title: This Dad Locked His Family In A Basement For 40 Days . . .

segments.say: This dad let his neighbor *die* outside his door, and his own daughter watched him do it.

segments.text: If you go out there, I'll kill you.

segments.say: But to understand why, we have to go back a few days.
Jack was a normal dad. Big house, nice car, and golf every *weekend*.
Then the TV said one thing. A *nuclear missile* was coming.
Jack grabbed his wife Anna and his daughter Lily, and ran *down* to the basement.
He locked the door. Then he *nailed* it shut with a hammer.
Lily screamed. Anna begged. But Jack kept hitting the nails, one by one.
Because outside, the *bomb* was coming.
The lights went out. In the dark, Lily asked if they were all going to *die*.
Jack said they only had to hold on for *two weeks*. After that, the radiation would be gone.
Anna wanted to call her parents. Jack said the lines were dead. But the phone rang. Grandma and grandpa were safe, in a *shelter*.
They had canned food, a little water, and a radio that did not work.
By day three, Jack and Anna were already *fighting*. About water. About money. About his golf.
Then, someone *knocked*.
It was their neighbor, Mrs. Park. She was crying. Her kids were *sick*.
Lily ran for the door. Anna told him to open it. Jack *refused*.
Mrs. Park kept knocking, slower and slower.
And then, the knocking *stopped*.
That night, nobody talked. Jack sat by the door and said sorry, over and over, to *no one*.
Lily never forgave him. She said those kids died in pain, and they could have *lived*.

segments.text: Dad did it to save our family.

segments.say: Day after day, it got worse. Food ran low. Then Lily heard her best friend was *dead*.
Grandma and grandpa called from a shelter. They were *sick* too.
Jack started counting every cup of water. Every can of food. Lily started counting the days on the *wall*.
But Jack noticed something weird. After a *nuclear* bomb, how was the phone still working?
Then he heard a *helicopter*.
The water was almost gone. So Jack did something smart. He caught the *dew* dripping from the ceiling.
Three and a half hours, for *one* cup.
Lily asked if it had *radiation* in it. Jack just smiled and said, try it.
Then the radio finally worked. And the news was worse than the bomb.
*North Korea* had taken the whole South. But the radiation outside had dropped.
So the family made *armor*. Snorkels, ski goggles, raincoats, and garden hats.
Jack even took a *selfie* before they went out. One, two, three.
He went up the stairs first. And the second he looked outside, his face *changed*.
He ran back down, screaming at them to get *down*.
Then everything went *black*.
When Lily woke up, Anna was *bleeding*. Glass everywhere.
Anna begged Lily to call grandma. The phone rang, and rang, and *rang*.
Back in the basement, Jack said the words nobody wanted to hear. Two more *weeks*.
Lily snapped.

segments.text: Open the door! Open the door now!

segments.say: And Anna finally said it out loud. This was all Jack's *fault*.
Jack screamed that he was the one keeping them alive. Anna just laughed in his *face*.
Then the itching started. Lily's skin turned *red*. Anna got a fever that would not go down.
One night, Lily said something that broke Jack.
Then Anna stopped *answering*.
Jack piled blankets on her. Lily held her hand. They kept telling each other she was *fine*.
Days passed. Anna did not *move*.
And then, one morning, Anna *opened* her eyes.
Jack hugged her. Lily cried. And Anna asked, how long has it been?
Jack *lied*. He said one day. But the wall was covered in marks.
So the family put their armor back on. Anna too.
They walked to the door together, and opened it to a *blinding* light.
But here is the thing. Did Anna really wake up? Or did Jack and Lily *lose their minds* down there?
Comment what you think was waiting outside that *door*.
